summary: Accepted ADR-001. OpenMOSS will be absorbed as a governance overlay, not as a replacement for the three-provinces/six-ministries semantic layer. Phase 1 storage is filesystem-first under ~/.openclaw/state/openmoss/, and install.sh remains out of scope through Wave 3.

Built task-core as an isolated server-side module with Task/Module/WorkItem entities, a guarded lifecycle state machine, and filesystem-first persistence under ~/.openclaw/state/openmoss/. Wave 2 intentionally stops before ActivityLog and public task APIs.

Built ActivityLog on top of task-core using JSONL event streams, then exposed minimal authenticated task APIs for list/create/get/timeline/claim/submit/review/block. Wave 3 stops before GUI work and before review/patrol subsystem specialization.

Built ReviewWorkflowService and ReviewRecord persistence so duchayuan-style approval is now a first-class state transition instead of a message-only convention. Review queue and per-task review history are queryable via API.

Built PatrolService and PatrolAlert persistence so stale tasks can be scanned, blocked, and surfaced with recovery guidance. Patrol now writes into the shared task state and ActivityLog instead of only existing as an implicit operator behavior.

Built a dedicated Governance tab in the GUI and connected it to the real OpenMOSS task APIs. The page now shows the task board, single-task timeline, review queue, and patrol alerts using live data, while leaving state-changing controls for Wave 6.
